unresolved.finding: Included Fortran sources are declared as library dependencies instead of object dependencies, so edits can relink the library without recompiling the affected code.
No prerequisite orders compilation of netcdf or netcdf4 after generation of the typeSizes module.
The convenience library generates .lo objects while module targets request separate .o objects from the same sources, allowing competing module-file generation.
The module targets provide no recipe to regenerate a missing module when the corresponding object remains up to date.
The cleanup list omits the uppercase module filenames explicitly supported by the installation rules.
Included Fortran files are prerequisites of the archive rather than its compiled objects, so changing an include can relink stale object code.
The build graph does not require the typeSizes module before compiling either netcdf object.
Module targets trigger ordinary .o compilation while the library independently triggers .lo compilation of the same sources, allowing concurrent writes to the same module files.
Module targets have prerequisites but no recovery recipes, so deleting a module while retaining its object does not cause regeneration.
CLEANFILES removes only lowercase module names even when the selected compiler generates uppercase module names.
The header installation loop does not stop on a failed copy, allowing successful installation of the second module to hide failure of the first.
Win32 and x64 configurations resolve mpi.lib from the same bundled x64 library directory without selecting an architecture-compatible alternative.
The project shares all configuration-specific intermediate directories with cxxpi, allowing compiler-generated database and log files to collide.
Both target architectures search the same bundled x64 directory for identically named MPI libraries, leaving the Win32 configurations with incompatible dependencies.
Intermediate directories contain no project identifier, leaving compiler-generated intermediate files vulnerable to collisions with sibling example projects using the same configuration directories.
Win32 and x64 configurations resolve fmpich2.lib from the same bundled x64 library directory without architecture-specific selection.
A nonempty user-supplied MPILIBS bypasses all link tests and is accepted after only a header compilation, even if its libraries cannot link MPI.
Repeated checks for different languages reuse nonempty MPILIBS without verifying that those libraries provide the new language's MPI bindings.
Compiler-wrapper discovery searches unprefixed executable names without distinguishing build-machine wrappers from target wrappers.
MPILIBS is documented as a user environment override but is not registered with AC_ARG_VAR for configure environment consistency checks.
The advertised --with-netcdf=DIR argument is passed directly to the linker instead of being converted into include and library search flags.
The macro generates Fortran test programs without selecting Fortran or documenting the required caller language.
An explicitly supplied library that fails detection remains in the exported LIBS_NETCDF variable despite the reported fallback to building without netCDF.
Several Fortran probes neither select the Fortran language nor document their dependence on the caller's current language.
The Fortran preprocessor defaults to the hardcoded /lib/cpp path and C-oriented options without checking availability or Fortran compatibility.
The LOC probe assigns an address to default-width INTEGER, potentially rejecting a supported intrinsic when pointer-width conversion warnings are fatal.
The repeatable line-length macros share one cache entry per language across different requested lengths and source formats.
The preprocessing test contains no code that requires preprocessing, allowing compilers that ignore directives and unknown options to produce a false positive.
Every preprocessing candidate is tested with the unprobed -Werror option, which can reject otherwise supported preprocessing flags.
The failure diagnostic says Fortran does do preprocessing when detection has failed.
All module names share ax_cv_fc_has_module, so subsequent module checks reuse the first module's result.
AX_FC_HAS_MODULE changes the current language without restoring it and does so only on cache misses.
The module check defines a preprocessor symbol but never assigns the shell variable used by AM_CONDITIONAL or the documented FC_HAS_MODULE output.
The macros claim DEFUN_ONCE protection against duplicate flags but are implemented with ordinary AC_DEFUN.
Failure while appending ltmain.sh exits only a subshell, allowing subsequent replacement and chmod commands to mask the generation failure.
The fallback AC_PROG_GO pushes the Go language without a corresponding language pop.
The Darwin undefined-symbol policy has no matching branch for explicit deployment targets beginning with 11 or later.
The Linux library-search configuration imports the build machine's /etc/ld.so.conf without a cross-compilation or sysroot guard.
The OS/2 branches assign old_archive_From_new_cmds with an uppercase F instead of the declared old_archive_from_new_cmds variable.
The OS/2 prefix_cmds string embeds shell quotes but is expanded as a command without eval, leaving those quotes literal in the sed arguments.
Several branches match the full host triplet against bare sysv4 or osf3 patterns, preventing their intended platform-specific handling.
The separated -L and -R flag test prefixes only its left operands with x, so those flags cannot match and their following directory arguments are lost.
_LT_UNLESS_OPTIONS is documented as testing whether all options are set, but its implementation suppresses the action when any option is set.
Unknown options only emit m4_warning although _LT_SET_OPTIONS promises to exit on an unknown option.
lt_combine pushes an _Lt_sep definition without a matching pop, leaving separator state on the m4 definition stack after each expansion.
Override variables are honored only when nonempty, so an explicitly empty CFLAGS or LIBS override still triggers pkg-config instead of honoring the documented override.
dep and depclean recurse into xbeachlibrary even though that Makefile.am comments out both targets, causing the forwarding targets to fail there.
Package metadata always appends a development tag and requests SVN revision tagging, leaving release and non-SVN version behavior dependent on legacy setuptools handling.
The executable omits NETCDF_FORTRAN_CFLAGS and NETCDF_FORTRAN_LIBS and instead hardcodes -lnetcdff, diverging from the library's discovered Fortran dependency settings.
The dependency recipe redirects into $(deps) without any local definition or guard, so an unset deps produces an invalid command and no module-order protection.
The executable post-build deletes the entire shared distribution directory, including library DLLs published by the library post-build scripts.
The previous distribution is removed before validating inputs and copy failures are unchecked, so a final successful license copy can conceal an incomplete package.
TargetDir is never cleared before wildcard packaging, allowing stale executables and DLLs from earlier builds to enter the new distribution.
Copy, directory-change, and archive failures are unchecked and can be hidden by the final successful deletion.
Adding into an existing ZIP does not remove entries whose source files disappeared, so repeated packaging can retain obsolete artifacts.
The script temporarily overwrites a destination 7za.exe and then deletes it unconditionally, with no distinction between its temporary copy and a pre-existing file.
Distribution commands pass directory macros unquoted, breaking argument boundaries for checkout paths containing spaces.
x64 netCDF Release objects and MPI_netcdf Debug objects, modules, and PDB files are directed into Win32 directories.
MPI_Release|x64 omits x64 from its static-library module include directory.
Combined MPI_netcdf configurations omit feature preprocessor definitions despite compiling against libraries built with both features enabled.
Win32 configurations select ifxCompiler despite the companion library retaining ifortCompiler for Win32, leaving the 32-bit compiler target unsupported or inconsistent.
Post-build distribution receives directory macros unquoted and therefore breaks for paths containing spaces.
Win32 MPI include lists separate the MPI and library paths with a space instead of the semicolon used elsewhere.
MPI paths assume include/mpi and lib directly below ONEAPI_ROOT without locating the MPI component installation.
Several x64 configurations write objects or modules into Win32 output directories, creating architecture collisions.
MPI_Release|x64 omits the x64 component from its static-library module search path.
Combined MPI_netcdf configurations enable preprocessing but omit MPI and netCDF definitions, unlike the corresponding static-library builds.
IFX executable builds reuse classic intermediate directories, permitting stale objects when switching compiler projects.
Only spacedecl.inc has a generation rule, so missing sibling generated includes are not recoverable when spacedecl.inc already exists.
version.dat has no prerequisites or forced refresh, so incremental rebuilds retain obsolete revision and build-date metadata.
SVN command failures occur inside successful echo recipes and can silently produce empty or invalid provenance fields.
The library lists interdependent Fortran sources while module dependency generation and inclusion are commented out, leaving parallel compilation ordering unspecified.
The library unconditionally supplies -fPIC despite the build scaffolding supporting compilers with different PIC flag conventions.
The netCDF branch unconditionally appends -lnetcdff after detected library variables, assuming a separately named Fortran library even when discovery selected another linkage layout.
CLEANFILES includes every local *.inc file and therefore removes the distributed nh_pars.inc during an in-source clean.
The source list names rainfall.F90 and bedroughness.F90 whereas the IDE projects name lowercase .f90 files, leaving case-sensitive builds with inconsistent source identities.
Deletion and XCOPY destination paths use raw unquoted %2, so space-containing target paths can be split or misinterpreted.
The ELSE belongs to the inner platform test, so a machine without Program Files (x86) never tries the documented default Program Files installation.
Existing MPICH files are removed before replacement succeeds, and failed local copies return immediately instead of trying bundled dependencies.
Platform is compared unquoted and unvalidated, so missing arguments produce malformed IF commands and unknown platforms fall through to Win32 dependencies.
Failure to copy common dependency DLLs is not checked before the netCDF copy can replace the command status.
COPY lacks an explicit overwrite policy, so repeated invocations depend on the inherited COPYCMD setting.
Only classic DLL filenames are accepted, although IFX callers default to project names containing IFX and therefore may produce no matching distribution input.
Both distributed DLLs are deleted before source existence or copy success is established, so missing inputs can erase previously usable artifacts without failing explicitly.
Each library's post-build invocation republishes both libraries from fixed directories while ignoring TargetDir, allowing stale counterpart binaries or concurrent post-build interference.
Neither the directory change nor generator execution is checked, and the final cd can hide generator failure from the caller.
The scripts-directory cd command has an opening quote without a closing quote, relying on permissive command parsing.
The script changes generic caller environment variables without SETLOCAL, leaving build-script state in the invoking shell.

Build_Date slices DATE at fixed character offsets, producing malformed dates under different Windows locale formats.
RevisionNumber is interpolated directly into an echoed Fortran literal without escaping, so quotes or command metacharacters can corrupt generation.
